svg.text: Power + USB data, no connectors. Dock board: hand-wired perfboard or a small PCB (same circuit). Wire colours are the physical wires; thin black lines are board tracks.
USB-A lead, cut and wired in
DOCK BOARD: perfboard or PCB in the receiver pocket, potted in clear epoxy
lead enters through a potted hole in the dock's lower edge
Q1 shorts D3 while charging. Perfboard: solder Q1, Q2 (SOT-23) and U3 (SOT-23-6) on with short wire legs.
Pin row 2: VBUS2 + GND2 bridged to VBUS and
GND on the pin strip (doubled power contacts);
SPARE1 + SPARE2 wired to 2 spare board pads.
contacts mate when the case is docked;
the printed snap holds it there
Opens when too hot: DET high,
charging off, red OFF LED on.
Status LEDs (3 mm, below the case):
No case: R3 holds Q2's gate high, so the pins carry no power.
Docked and cool: the case grounds DET through the thermostat, Q2 turns on, DOCK lights.
Too hot, short (F1 trips) or bad contact: VBUS_OUT is off while PRESENT is grounded, so OFF lights.
USB data passes straight through. If the phone charges slowly from your bike charger, solder JP1 shut.
